subject.title: fix(codex): restore native PreToolUse relay delivery

question: Should OpenClaw accept this positive-delivery Codex path before the packaged Codex runtime independently proves Code Mode PreToolUse emission, and with policy-active sessions forced onto unified exec plus fresh-thread binding refresh?
rationale: This choice changes a tool-execution security boundary and upgrade behavior, so code review can identify the blockers but cannot choose the product/security tradeoff for maintainers.

options.title: Fix Then Decide Runtime Gate
options.body: First repair the code_mode_exec policy normalization, then keep the draft paused until maintainers explicitly accept or prove the Codex runtime prerequisite and unified-exec/fresh-thread tradeoff.

options.title: Accept The Tradeoff After Proof
options.body: Maintainers can accept the compatibility and runtime dependency risk if they verify the packaged Codex version emits the needed PreToolUse event and the upgrade behavior is acceptable.

options.title: Prefer A Different Draft
options.body: Maintainers can pause or close this PR in favor of one of the related fail-closed or broader native-surface enforcement drafts if that security posture is preferred.

recommendation.title: Fix Then Decide Runtime Gate
recommendation.body: First repair the code_mode_exec policy normalization, then keep the draft paused until maintainers explicitly accept or prove the Codex runtime prerequisite and unified-exec/fresh-thread tradeoff.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent no-policy native hook fallback and documentation work makes this the best available owner for the security/compatibility decision.
